method.model: ONE electrical load, explicitly declared by the inventor, that behaves as a single constant resistance R_load (in ohms) under ONE steady DC voltage V_load (in volts) across it for ONE declared duration t (in seconds), so that the power it absorbs stays constant throughout that duration. V_load is signed and is measured from the load terminal the inventor calls + to the terminal they call −. Under the passive sign convention (current taken through the load from + to −) the load absorbs the power P_load = V_load² / R_load, and a power that stays constant throughout t transfers the energy E_load (in joules) = P_load × t, so E_load = V_load² × t / R_load: never negative for a positive resistance and a duration that is not negative, exactly zero for a zero voltage or a zero duration and the same for +V and −V. The result is the theoretical absorbed energy of that ideal relation only, not a measured, rated, stored, available or guaranteed energy, not a battery capacity, charge or runtime and not a temperature.
method.executed_form: e_load = v_load^2 x t_duration / r_load, with v_load in V (signed), r_load in ohm (strictly positive) and t_duration in s (not negative), the sign of r_load and of t_duration decided from the exact decimal values before any binary rounding; evaluated as the exact rational value of the three binary64 inputs rounded once to binary64 and accepted only when it is exactly 0.0 for a zero voltage or a zero duration, or finite, positive and within a relative error of 2^-52 of it; then shown only when it agrees with the exact decimal value V^2 x t / R of the entered values within a relative error of 2^-50, as that exact value rounded once to 12 significant digits (round half to even) and labelled exact or rounded.
method.derivation: DOE-HDBK-1011/1-92, Electrical Science, Volume 1, Module 1, gives Ohm's law, E = I x R (handbook page 14), and electric power, P = I x E (handbook page 16), with E the voltage in volts, I the current in amperes, R the resistance in ohms and P the power in watts (DOE-ENG-S1; recorded as electronics_electrical:PR004). DOE-HDBK-1010-92, Classical Physics, Module CP-05, defines power as the rate at which energy is transferred or used (printed page 8; DOE-ENG-S2; recorded as electronics_electrical:PR008). InventorAI writes the voltage as V, substitutes I = V / R into P = V x I to obtain P = V^2 / R for a resistance greater than zero, and, ONLY for a power that stays constant throughout the declared duration t, restates that definition as E = P x t, so E = V^2 x t / R; neither handbook is claimed to print these combined forms or the passive sign convention, which are InventorAI's own statement, and no varying-power, average-power or integration treatment is derived. The joule and the second, and J = W x s, follow the SI units identified in NIST SP 811 (NIST-JS-S1; recorded as electronics_electrical:PR009). The relations are restated independently; no handbook text, worked example, figure or table is copied, no textbook material is reproduced, and the relation is not shown to describe the inventor's load.

rules: Grammar: strict ASCII decimal - an optional single leading minus, one to nine integer digits for V and t or one to twelve for R, and an optional single fractional part of one to nine digits; no plus sign, exponent, separator, space, Unicode digit, unit suffix, inf, nan or normalization. An omitted, malformed or over-length value is INVALID_NUMERIC_INPUT, resolved before the shared owner is called.

Representation limits, not physical limits: the digit limits bound what can be typed (|V| below 10^9 V, R from 10^-9 to below 10^12 ohm, t from 0 to below 10^9 s, steps of 10^-9); they are not physical limits, equipment ratings, operating times or a claim that such values are realistic, and the 64-character field cap is NON-PHYSICAL abuse protection only.

Positive resistance, then duration not negative: the exact decimal value of R must be greater than zero (otherwise RESISTANCE_NOT_POSITIVE), and then the exact decimal value of t must not be negative (otherwise DURATION_NEGATIVE), each decided before any binary rounding and with no number. A zero voltage or a zero duration, including -0, is admitted and gives exactly zero energy, never a negative zero.

Owner applicability: the shared owner declines an r_load that is not greater than zero as UNABLE_TO_DETERMINE / INPUT_OUTSIDE_ADMITTED_RANGE, shown as the neutral UNMAPPED_OWNER_OUTCOME (unreachable from the page); a negative t_duration is refused by the method adapter as FAILURE / EXECUTION_INTEGRITY_FAILURE (unreachable from the page).

Binary bridge: each admitted decimal is converted once to the correctly rounded binary64 value; every admitted nonzero value lies between 10^-9 and 10^12 in magnitude, so it is a normal binary64 number with a relative rounding error of at most 2^-53, a positive R stays positive, a duration that is not negative stays not negative and a zero V or t stays exactly zero.

Numerical acceptance in the adapter: the exact rational value v_load^2 x t_duration / r_load of the binary inputs is rounded once to binary64. A zero voltage or a zero duration gives exactly 0.0. A nonzero exact result is accepted only when the rounded value is finite, positive and within a relative error of 2^-52 of it; overflow, underflow or any failed check is FAILURE / EXECUTION_INTEGRITY_FAILURE with no numerical payload, never rewritten as a refusal. Inside the representation limits every nonzero result lies between 10^-39 and 10^36 J, so neither overflow nor underflow can occur from the page.

Decimal-reference acceptance in the consumer: a successful owner result is shown only when it is exactly zero (not a negative zero) for an exactly zero voltage or duration, and otherwise is positive and lies within a relative error of 2^-50 of the exact decimal value V^2 x t / R of the entered decimals; otherwise the outcome is KNOWLEDGE_UNAVAILABLE with no number. The proven worst case for every admitted input is below 5.0000001 x 2^-53.

Display: the accepted result is shown from the exact decimal value, never from the binary value: rounded once to 12 significant digits, round half to even, with trailing zeros removed; it is labelled exact when that rounding changes nothing and rounded otherwise. Plain decimal notation is used from 10^-6 J to below 10^12 J and the form m x 10^e otherwise, so a tiny nonzero energy is never shown as 0. The digits shown imply no measurement resolution, precision or accuracy.

disclosure: This is the theoretical electrical energy that one resistive load absorbs over the duration t you declared, at the steady DC voltage V and with the resistance R you declared, while its power stays constant: E = V² × t / R = P × t, where P = V² / R.

Sign: V is the voltage across the load from the terminal you called + to the terminal you called −, and the current is taken through the load in the same direction. The load then absorbs E, which is never negative, is the same for a positive or a negative V, and is zero when V or t is zero.

The voltage, resistance and duration are your own declared values. InventorAI did not measure them and does not check that the load is resistive, that its resistance and voltage stay constant or that the power stays constant for the whole duration.

It is the ideal steady-state, constant-power relation only: a power that changes during the duration, on-off or duty-cycled use, wiring and contact resistance, the source's internal resistance and voltage drop, a battery voltage that falls as it discharges, temperature change of the resistance, start-up or inrush current, switching, AC behaviour, conversion losses and non-resistive loads such as motors, lamps, LEDs or electronics are not included.
The value is shown exactly when it can be; otherwise it is rounded to 12 significant digits and labelled rounded. The digits follow from your entry; they are not the precision of any measurement.

Next engineering need: this energy is not a battery capacity, a runtime or a temperature. Whether any battery or source can supply this energy and this power, how long a real source would last, how hot the load or its surroundings become, whether the load, its resistor, wiring, source and any driver or switch are rated for it, and what protection the circuit needs all remain unverified, and must be checked by measurement or a qualified person before any reliance.
